domain: EU food-safety scientific assessment / EFSA health-claim opinion outcome prediction (claim-level regulatory-outcome task, EU agency + Commission publisher pair)

jurisdiction.publisher: European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) for the claims corpus and opinions; Directorate-General for Health and Food Safety (DG SANTE, European Commission) for the EU Register of Nutrition and Health Claims

prediction_question: For a health claim submitted to EFSA under Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006 - either a general-function claim (Art. 13.1) from the Member State list, or an application (Art. 13.5 / Art. 14) received via a national competent authority - will EFSA's NDA Panel conclude that a cause-and-effect relationship is established (favourable opinion), rather than not established (unfavourable)?
prediction_time: For Art. 13.5/14 applications: the instant EFSA receives/validates the application (published per the Transparency Regulation regime on OpenEFSA); the Panel 'shall' adopt its opinion within 5 months excluding stop-the-clock periods (EFSA guidance). For the Art. 13.1 batch: the compilation of the Member State claim list (4,637 main entries, published as the EFSA claims database, 2010) precedes the Panel's wave evaluations (2009-2011). Features are the submitted claim content only: claim wording, food/constituent, claimed effect, target group, conditions of use, article route, applicant identity (13.5/14). NOT YET WORKED AS A DATED EXAMPLE - one OpenEFSA-record worked example (application receipt instant vs opinion adoption date, with the feature window in between) is a named open item below.
target_definition: Binary: favourable vs unfavourable Panel conclusion on the claim. Label source: the published EFSA Journal opinion's conclusion ('a cause and effect relationship has [not] been established'), cross-checkable against the Commission's EU Register of Nutrition and Health Claims (authorised vs non-authorised status + reasons). Label source columns are excludable from shipped features; the register/opinion fields that carry the outcome are not features.

2026-11-06: the register and OpenEFSA channels were measured anonymously end-to-end; the FIP register is DG SANTE Commission content (CC BY 4.0 site notice quoted above), OpenEFSA is EFSA content under its attribution notice. Wiley-hosted opinions render in-browser; the per-document copyright line inside each opinion remains unextracted (the only open licence item, moot after the drop verdict).
split_strategy: Candidate (counts not yet measured from the source - the named gap): temporal split at opinion-adoption level, train = Art 13.1 batch opinions (2009-2011) + early Art 13.5/14 applications (2008-2015), eval = 2016-2020, holdout = 2021-2025. Positives cluster by opinion: one NDA Panel opinion can decide dozens of Art 13.1 claims at once, so claim rows within one opinion are NOT independent and the clustered (opinion-level) count must be recorded with the claim-level count. Published publisher statistics (cross-check evidence, not a measured panel): 2,758 general-function claims assessed by 28 July 2011 with 'about one in five' favourable (EFSA press news 110728); Art 13.5/14 applications finalised by Nov 2013: 91 (13 positive / 78 negative) and 100 (33 positive / 67 negative) (EFSA NDA presentation, document 131120-p03.pdf) - roughly 20-33% favourable depending on route.

measurements.extraction_cost_2026_11_06: Register: 1 request, 19,885,668 bytes, ~6s coordinator-side (single bulk JSON; per-claim details endpoint /policy-items/POL-HC-11221 = 8,280 B/claim if needed). OpenEFSA: ~1 request per (filter, year) at ~120 KB each (limit=1 + facets), or the full question set by paging 20-100/call; timeline 1 request/question. Opinion conclusions: 1 page/opinion through a browser channel (Wiley).

rejection_reason: DROPPED on split capacity (2026-11-06, all counts measured, commands in notes.md): the task population cannot fill disjoint train/eval/holdout windows with enough independent positives. (1) The Commission register (FIP backend, one anonymous 19,885,668-byte JSON call, 2,337 published claims) splits into an Art 13.1 batch decided in opinion waves 2009-2012 (2,069 claims: 2009 95/312, 2010 89/663, 2011 40/826, 2012 2/39, 2015 2/0 auth/non-auth; all submitted as ONE 2008-2010 cohort - OpenEFSA shows 4,430 health-claim questions received in 2008 and 481 in 2010) and a thin Art 13.5/14 stream: 267 register-decided claims across 2008-2022, of which 41 authorised; after 2015 the register shows 36 decided 13.5/14 claims with 2 positives total (2016-2022), and OpenEFSA measures the whole post-2020 application stream at 22 received (2021-2026) of which 14 published - the stream is ending, not flowing. (2) Chronological integrity forbids the 13.1 cohort as holdout: its prediction instant (list compilation, 2008-2010) precedes the train window's outcomes. Every defensible temporal holdout therefore carries <=36 rows and <=3 independent positives - a scored holdout CI would be noise. (3) Withdrawal censoring compounds it: recent 13.5/14 years show withdrawals rivalling decisions (2018: 7 withdrawn vs 4 published; 2019: 7 vs 3). (4) Label cost rose too: measured divergence - claim POL-HC-11221 (isomaltulose/BENEO, Q-2021-00073) has a FAVOURABLE Panel conclusion ('a cause and effect relationship has been established', adopted 2021-09-15, published 2021-10-20) yet register status Non-authorised (reason HC_RR_166: no conditions of use possible), so labels must be extracted per opinion (Wiley pages render in the supported browser; plain HTTP is 403) and cannot be taken from register status. REOPENS IF: a new EU regulatory route revives application volume (hundreds of decided claims per year reaching a fresh window), or the task is redesigned to a population with an ongoing multi-year flow - e.g. the sibling novel-foods application stream (separate lead, unopened). Licence (EFSA attribution notice + Commission CC BY 4.0), access (register bulk JSON + OpenEFSA x-security API + in-browser Wiley) and novelty (no_precedent, checked 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-06) are all RESOLVED as recorded evidence - the blocker is the population, not permission or access.
review: Access, licence, timing and novelty all resolved 2026-11-06 with recorded evidence; the decisive blocker is split capacity: the Art 13.1 batch is one 2008-2010 cohort decided in 2009-2012 waves, and the 13.5/14 application stream is small and ending (22 received applications 2021-2026, 14 decided; 2 favourable outcomes in the register for all of 2016-2022), so no temporal holdout window carries enough independent positives to be scored. Labels additionally require per-opinion extraction (favourable opinion vs non-authorised register divergence measured on POL-HC-11221).
next_action: Dropped 2026-11-06 on split capacity (see rejection_reason; all probes reproducible via candidates/efsa-health-claim-opinion-outcome/probe_fip_register.py and probe_openefsa.py). Reopening event: a new regulatory route reviving decided-claim volume into fresh years, or a redesigned task on a population with ongoing flow - the novel-foods application stream (Reg (EU) 2015/2283, applications list legally public per Art 10; FIP novel-food screen carries only the 33-item Union list; the application-status join OpenEFSA-question -> Union-list authorisation is the unmeasured next probe) is the natural sibling and remains an UNOPENED lead, not this candidate.
